questions.setting: Imagine that a Canadian marketing firm is doing research in your country. You have agreed to participate in a telephone interview about coffee shops.
questions: How often do you go to a coffee shop, and who do you usually go with?
What do you usually order at a coffee shop?
Do you prefer to go to a big chain coffee shop or a small local coffee shop? Why?
models: I go to a coffee shop about three times a week. I usually go with my coworkers after lunch. It's a good way to take a short break.
I usually order an iced Americano. It's not too expensive, and it helps me stay awake. Sometimes I also get a small cake. I usually get a large size.

I prefer big chain coffee shops. There are two reasons. First, they are everywhere, so it's easy to find one. For example, there are three chain coffee shops near my office. Second, the taste is always the same, so I don't have to worry. Also, they have free Wi-Fi and many seats. That's why I prefer big chain coffee shops.
modelsIH: I go to a coffee shop almost every weekday, usually right after lunch. Most of the time, I go with my coworkers, because it's a nice chance to chat and relax before the afternoon.
I usually order an iced Americano, even in winter. It's simple, it's cheaper than other drinks, and it really helps me focus. If I'm hungry, I sometimes add a muffin or a sandwich.

I prefer big chain coffee shops for two main reasons. First, they're really convenient. There are several near my office, so I can grab a coffee anytime. Second, the quality is consistent, so I always know what I'm going to get. On top of that, they usually have free Wi-Fi and comfortable seats, which is great when I need to work. So, overall, chain coffee shops suit my lifestyle better.
modelsAL: I'd say I go to a coffee shop almost every weekday, usually right after lunch. I tend to go with a couple of coworkers, since it gives us a chance to unwind and catch up before the afternoon gets busy.
I usually go for an iced Americano, even in the middle of winter. It's simple, reasonably priced, and it gives me the energy boost I need. If I skipped lunch, I'll grab a sandwich as well.

Honestly, I lean toward big chain coffee shops. The main reason is convenience. There are several within walking distance of my office, so I never have to go out of my way. Besides, the quality is consistent, so I know exactly what I'm paying for. Small local cafés can be charming, but they're often crowded and hard to find a seat in. For someone with a busy schedule like me, chains are simply more practical.
keyPhrases: I go to ... about three times a week.

opinions.question: Do you agree or disagree with the following statement? It is better to work for a large company than a small company. Give specific reasons and examples to support your opinion.
opinions.model: I agree that it's better to work for a large company. There are two reasons. First, large companies usually pay more. They also give good benefits, like health insurance and bonuses. Second, there are more chances to learn. For example, my friend works at a big electronics company. The company gives free English classes and computer training. Because of this, he got promoted quickly. On the other hand, small companies often don't have the money for training. Also, a large company is more stable, so I don't have to worry about losing my job. That's why I think it's better to work for a large company.
opinions.modelIH: I agree that it's better to work for a large company, for two main reasons. First, large companies usually offer higher salaries and better benefits, such as health insurance, bonuses, and longer vacations. This makes employees feel secure. Second, there are many more opportunities to learn and grow. For example, my friend works at a big electronics company. The company offers free English classes, leadership training, and even chances to work overseas. Thanks to this, he improved his skills a lot and got promoted within three years. Small companies, on the other hand, often can't afford this kind of training. Of course, small companies can have a friendly atmosphere, but for my career, I think a large company is the better choice. That's why I agree with the statement.
opinions.modelAL: I agree that working for a large company is generally the better option, especially early in your career. The most obvious advantage is financial security. Large firms tend to offer higher salaries and more generous benefits, like health insurance, performance bonuses, and paid leave. Beyond that, they invest heavily in their employees' development. A friend of mine works for a major electronics company, and over the past three years he's taken free language courses, completed leadership training, and even spent six months at the overseas branch. That kind of experience accelerated his career in a way a small firm probably couldn't. Admittedly, small companies can offer a closer-knit atmosphere and more responsibility. But overall, the stability and growth opportunities of a large company make it the smarter choice.

opinions.question: Which do you prefer: studying alone or studying in a group? Give specific reasons and examples to support your opinion.
opinions.model: I prefer studying alone. There are two reasons. First, I can focus better. When I study with other people, we often talk about other things and waste time. Second, I can study at my own speed. For example, when I prepared for the TOEIC test last year, I studied alone at the library every evening. I spent more time on the parts that were difficult for me, like listening. Because of this, I got a good score. In a group, I have to follow other people's speed. Also, the library is quiet, so I can concentrate for a long time. That's why I prefer studying alone.

Group study can be useful for discussing difficult concepts, but for steady, focused progress, nothing beats studying alone.

Actually, I talked about this experience in my job interview, and it helped me a lot. That's why I think volunteer work should be required.
opinions.modelAL: I agree that volunteer work should be part of every student's education. Most students spend their days focused on grades and exams, and volunteering exposes them to a side of society they might otherwise never see. It builds empathy in a way no classroom lesson can. It also gives them practical experience. In high school, I volunteered at a nursing home once a month. Honestly, I was reluctant at first, but over time I came to really enjoy chatting with the residents and helping out at lunch. I learned how to communicate with patience and respect, skills that turned out to be valuable later. In fact, I talked about that experience in a job interview, and the interviewer seemed genuinely impressed. Making it a requirement simply ensures every student gets that opportunity.

opinions.question: What is the most important quality of a good manager? Choose one of the following and explain why: being a good listener, being organized, or being friendly. Give specific reasons and examples to support your opinion.
opinions.model: I think being a good listener is the most important quality of a good manager. There are two reasons. First, if a manager listens well, employees can share their ideas freely. Second, the manager can find problems early. For example, my old manager always listened to our opinions in meetings. One time, I said our work process was too slow. He listened and changed it, and our team became much faster. Everyone felt respected. Also, when employees feel respected, they work harder for the team. That's why I think being a good listener is the most important quality.
opinions.modelIH: In my opinion, being a good listener is the most important quality of a good manager. First, when a manager really listens, employees feel comfortable sharing their ideas and concerns. This creates a positive team atmosphere. Second, a manager who listens can find and solve problems early. For example, my former manager always asked for our opinions at weekly meetings and listened carefully. One day, I mentioned that our report process had too many steps. He listened, discussed it with the team, and simplified the process. As a result, we saved several hours every week, and everyone felt respected. Being organized and friendly are also good, but without listening, a manager can't understand the team. That's why listening is the most important.
opinions.modelAL: Of the three, I believe being a good listener matters most. A manager who genuinely listens makes employees feel valued, and that encourages them to speak up with ideas and concerns. It also means problems surface early, before they grow into something serious. My former manager was a great example. At every weekly meeting, he'd ask for our input and actually take notes. Once, I pointed out that our reporting process involved too many unnecessary steps. Instead of brushing it off, he discussed it with the team and simplified the whole system, which saved us several hours a week. More than that, it showed us our opinions mattered. Organization and friendliness are certainly helpful, but a manager who doesn't listen will never truly understand their team.
keyPhrases: I think ... is the most important quality.
Employees can share their ideas freely.
keyPhrasesAL: Of the three, I believe ... matters most.

opinions.question: Do you agree or disagree with the following statement? It is better to live in a city than in the countryside. Give specific reasons and examples to support your opinion.
opinions.model: I agree that it's better to live in a city. There are two reasons. First, cities are very convenient. There are many stores, hospitals, and restaurants nearby. Second, public transportation is good. For example, I live in Seoul, and there is a subway station five minutes from my house. I can go anywhere easily without a car. When I visited my grandparents in the countryside, I had to drive thirty minutes to buy groceries. Also, there are more jobs in the city. Also, cities have many fun things to do, like concerts and festivals. That's why I think living in a city is better.
opinions.modelIH: I agree that it's better to live in a city, mainly for two reasons. First, cities are much more convenient. Everything you need, like supermarkets, hospitals, banks, and restaurants, is close by. Second, public transportation is excellent. For example, I live in Seoul, and there's a subway station just five minutes from my apartment. I can get to work, meet friends, or go shopping easily without a car. On the other hand, when I visit my grandparents in the countryside, we have to drive thirty minutes just to buy groceries, and there are only a few buses a day. In addition, cities have many more job opportunities and cultural activities. Of course, the countryside is quieter, but for daily life, the city is better.
opinions.modelAL: For me, city life is clearly the better option. Convenience is the biggest factor. In a city, almost everything you need, from supermarkets and hospitals to banks and restaurants, is within easy reach. Public transportation is another major advantage. I live in Seoul, and there's a subway station just five minutes from my apartment, so I can get practically anywhere without a car. Compare that to my grandparents' village, where buying groceries means a thirty-minute drive and buses come only a few times a day. Cities also offer far more job opportunities, not to mention concerts, museums, and other cultural activities. The countryside certainly has its charm, with cleaner air and a slower pace, but for everyday living, the city is hard to beat.

opinions.question: Do you agree or disagree with the following statement? Companies should allow employees to choose their own working hours. Give specific reasons and examples to support your opinion.
opinions.model: I agree that companies should let employees choose their working hours. There are two reasons. First, employees can balance work and life. For example, parents can take their children to school in the morning. Second, people can work when they focus best. Some people work better in the morning, and others work better in the afternoon. My company started flexible hours last year. Now I start at seven and finish at four. I feel less tired, and my work is better. Also, people can avoid rush hour, so they spend less time on the road. That's why I agree with this statement.
opinions.modelIH: I agree that companies should allow employees to choose their own working hours, for two main reasons. First, it helps employees balance their work and personal lives. For example, parents can drop their children off at school in the morning and still work a full day. Second, people can work when they are most productive. Some people focus best early in the morning, while others work better in the afternoon. My company introduced flexible hours last year. Now I start at seven and leave at four, so I avoid rush hour traffic and have more time in the evening. As a result, I feel less stressed, and I actually get more done. Of course, teams need some common hours for meetings, but overall, flexible hours are good for both employees and companies.
opinions.modelAL: I strongly agree that employees should have some control over their working hours. For one thing, it allows people to manage their personal responsibilities without sacrificing their careers. A parent, for example, could drop the kids off at school and still put in a full day. For another, not everyone does their best work at the same time of day. Some people are sharpest at dawn, while others hit their stride in the afternoon. My company introduced flexible hours last year, and I now work from seven to four. Avoiding rush hour alone has made a huge difference to my energy levels, and I'm noticeably more productive. Naturally, teams still need a few core hours for meetings and collaboration. But within that framework, flexibility benefits everyone, including the company.
keyPhrases: Employees can balance work and life.
People can work when they focus best.

opinions.question: What are the advantages and disadvantages of using social media? Give specific reasons and examples to support your opinion.
opinions.model: There are advantages and disadvantages of using social media. The biggest advantage is that we can stay in touch with people easily. For example, my best friend lives in Canada, but we talk on social media every week. I can see her photos and news. However, there is also a big disadvantage. People can spend too much time on it. For example, I sometimes look at my phone for two hours before bed, and then I can't sleep well. Some people also feel bad when they compare their lives with others. So I think social media is useful, but we should use it carefully.
opinions.modelIH: Social media has both advantages and disadvantages. The biggest advantage is that it's easy to stay connected with people, even if they live far away. For example, my best friend moved to Canada three years ago, but we still keep in touch through social media. I can see her photos and comment on her posts, so I feel like she's still close to me. It's also a fast way to get news and information. However, there's a serious disadvantage. It's very easy to waste time. For example, I sometimes scroll through videos for two hours before bed without realizing it, and then I can't sleep well. Some people also feel bad when they compare their lives with others' posts. So I think social media is helpful, but we need to set limits.
opinions.modelAL: Social media is a double-edged sword. On the positive side, it makes staying connected incredibly easy. My best friend moved to Canada three years ago, yet thanks to social media, I still feel involved in her life. I see her photos, react to her updates, and we message almost daily. It's also a quick way to keep up with news and trends. On the downside, it can be extremely addictive. I'll admit I've lost entire evenings scrolling through short videos, only to realize it's past midnight and I can't fall asleep. Another concern is that constantly comparing ourselves to the carefully edited lives of others can hurt our self-esteem. So while social media has real value, I think it's important to use it intentionally and set clear limits.

However, there is also a big disadvantage.

keyPhrasesIH: It's also a fast way to ...
keyPhrasesAL: On the positive side, ... On the downside, ...

opinions.question: Some people prefer to spend money on experiences, such as travel or concerts. Others prefer to spend money on things, such as clothes or electronics. Which do you prefer? Give specific reasons and examples to support your opinion.
opinions.model: I prefer to spend money on experiences. There are two reasons. First, experiences make good memories that last forever. Things get old or broken, but memories stay. Second, experiences help me relax. For example, two years ago, I spent my bonus on a trip to Japan with my family. We still talk about the food and the hot springs. But I don't even remember what I bought with my bonus the year before. Also, I can share these experiences with my family and friends. That's why I prefer to spend money on experiences.
opinions.modelIH: I prefer to spend money on experiences rather than things, for two reasons. First, experiences create memories that last a lifetime. Things like clothes or phones get old, break, or go out of style, but good memories stay with us. Second, experiences help me relax and learn something new. For example, two years ago, I used my year-end bonus to take my parents on a trip to Japan. We tried local food, visited a traditional hot spring, and took lots of photos. Even now, we often talk about that trip at family dinners, and it always makes us smile. On the other hand, I can't even remember what I bought with my bonus the year before. That's why I think experiences are a better use of money.
opinions.modelAL: I'd much rather spend money on experiences than on possessions. The main reason is that experiences tend to stay with us far longer. A new phone or a stylish jacket feels exciting for a few weeks, but eventually it becomes outdated or worn out. Memories, on the other hand, often become more meaningful over time. Two years ago, I used my year-end bonus to take my parents to Japan. We explored local markets, relaxed in a traditional hot spring, and laughed our way through a lot of unfamiliar dishes. To this day, that trip comes up at almost every family dinner. By contrast, I honestly couldn't tell you what I bought with my bonus the year before. That contrast says it all: experiences are simply a better investment in happiness.

opinions.question: Do you agree or disagree with the following statement? High school students should have part-time jobs. Give specific reasons and examples to support your opinion.
opinions.model: I disagree that high school students should have part-time jobs. There are two reasons. First, students need time to study. High school is very important for their future. Second, they need time to rest. For example, my cousin worked at a convenience store when he was in high school. He worked three nights a week, so he was always tired in class. His grades went down a lot. Students will have many years to work later. Also, part-time jobs for students usually don't pay very much. That's why I disagree with this statement.
opinions.modelIH: I disagree that high school students should have part-time jobs, mainly for two reasons. First, high school students need to focus on their studies. Their grades in high school can decide which university they go to, so this time is very important. Second, students need enough rest and free time to stay healthy. For example, my cousin worked at a convenience store three nights a week when he was a high school student. He wanted to earn pocket money, but he was always exhausted and often fell asleep in class. In the end, his grades dropped, and he regretted it. Of course, working can teach responsibility, but students can learn that through volunteering or school activities. They will have plenty of time to work later in life.
opinions.modelAL: I don't think high school students should have part-time jobs, at least not during the school year. High school is a critical period academically. The grades students earn can shape which universities and opportunities are open to them later. Adding a job to an already demanding schedule can easily push their studies aside. Rest matters too. Teenagers need enough sleep and downtime to stay healthy. My cousin is a good example. He worked night shifts at a convenience store three times a week to earn some pocket money. Before long, he was constantly exhausted, dozing off in class, and his grades slipped significantly, which he still regrets. Admittedly, a job can teach responsibility, but students can develop that through volunteering or school clubs. After all, they'll have decades of working life ahead of them.

opinions.question: Which is a better way to learn about a new city: taking a guided tour or exploring on your own? Give specific reasons and examples to support your opinion.
opinions.model: I think exploring on my own is better. There are two reasons. First, I can go anywhere I want. I don't have to follow a schedule. Second, I can find special places. For example, when I visited Bangkok, I walked around without a plan. I found a small local restaurant, and the food was amazing. It was not in any guidebook. On a guided tour, I can only see famous places with many tourists. Also, I can save money because guided tours are usually expensive. That's why I think exploring on my own is better.
opinions.modelIH: I think exploring on my own is a better way to learn about a new city, for two reasons. First, I have the freedom to go wherever I want and stay as long as I like. On a guided tour, I have to follow a fixed schedule, so I can't spend extra time at places I really like. Second, I can discover hidden places that most tourists don't know about. For example, when I visited Bangkok last year, I spent a whole day walking around without a plan. I found a tiny local restaurant in an alley, and the noodles were the best I've ever had. I also chatted with the owner and learned about the neighborhood. That's something I could never experience on a guided tour.
opinions.modelAL: For me, exploring on my own is by far the better way to get to know a new city. The biggest draw is freedom. I can linger at places that fascinate me and skip the ones that don't, rather than being rushed along by a tour guide's schedule. More importantly, wandering without a plan often leads to the most memorable discoveries. When I was in Bangkok last year, I spent an entire day just walking through different neighborhoods. Down a narrow alley, I stumbled upon a tiny family-run noodle shop, and it turned out to be the best meal of the whole trip. The owner even gave me tips on local spots to visit. Guided tours are efficient for seeing major landmarks, but they rarely show you the real character of a city.
keyPhrases: I can go anywhere I want.

opinions.question: Do you agree or disagree with the following statement? Technology has made people's lives less stressful. Give specific reasons and examples to support your opinion.
opinions.model: I disagree that technology has made our lives less stressful. There are two reasons. First, we are always connected to work. We get work emails and messages even at night. Second, we get too much information. For example, my manager sometimes sends me messages on weekends, and I feel like I have to answer right away. So I can't really rest. Also, I check the news on my phone all the time, and it makes me worried. Also, we check our phones all day, so it's hard to relax. That's why I think technology has made our lives more stressful.
opinions.modelIH: I disagree that technology has made people's lives less stressful, for two reasons. First, because of smartphones, we're always connected to work. In the past, people could forget about work when they left the office, but now we get emails and messages anytime. For example, my manager often sends messages on weekends, and I feel pressure to reply right away. As a result, I never feel completely free. Second, we're exposed to too much information. We check news, social media, and notifications all day, and this makes it hard to relax and focus. Of course, technology makes some tasks easier, like banking or shopping. But overall, I think it has added more stress to our lives than it has removed.
opinions.modelAL: I'd have to disagree. Although technology has made many tasks more convenient, I think it's made our lives more stressful overall. The biggest issue is that it's blurred the line between work and personal time. Not long ago, leaving the office meant leaving work behind. Now, with smartphones, we're reachable around the clock. My manager, for instance, frequently sends messages on weekends, and even when nothing is urgent, I feel obliged to respond immediately. It's hard to truly switch off. On top of that, we're bombarded with a constant stream of notifications, news alerts, and social media updates, which makes it difficult to relax or concentrate. Technology certainly saves time on things like banking and shopping, but the mental cost of being always on is significant.
keyPhrases: We are always connected to work.
keyPhrasesAL: it's blurred the line between ... and ...
It's hard to truly switch off.

opinions.question: Some people think that the government should spend more money on public transportation. Others think the money should be spent on building more roads. Which do you agree with? Give specific reasons and examples to support your opinion.
opinions.model: I think the government should spend more money on public transportation. There are two reasons. First, it helps reduce traffic. One bus can carry many people, so there are fewer cars on the road. Second, it's better for the environment. For example, in my city, a new subway line opened two years ago. After that, many people stopped driving to work. Traffic got better, and the air became cleaner. More roads just bring more cars. Also, public transportation helps people who can't drive, like students and old people. That's why I think public transportation is a better choice.
opinions.modelIH: I believe the government should spend more money on public transportation rather than roads, for two reasons. First, public transportation is more effective at reducing traffic. One bus or subway train can carry hundreds of people, which means far fewer cars on the road. Building more roads usually just encourages more people to drive. Second, it's much better for the environment. For example, a new subway line opened in my city two years ago. Since then, many of my coworkers have stopped driving to work. The traffic downtown is lighter, and the air feels cleaner. It also helps people who can't drive, like students and the elderly. That's why I think investing in public transportation is the smarter choice.
opinions.modelAL: I'm firmly on the side of investing in public transportation. The main reason is efficiency. A single subway train can move hundreds of people at once, taking a huge number of cars off the road. Building new roads, on the other hand, often just attracts more drivers, so congestion returns within a few years. There's also a strong environmental case. Fewer cars mean lower emissions and cleaner air, which benefits everyone. My own city is a good example. When a new subway line opened two years ago, many of my coworkers stopped driving, and the downtown traffic has noticeably eased. Public transportation also serves people who can't drive, such as students, the elderly, and people with disabilities. For all these reasons, it's a far better long-term investment than more roads.
keyPhrasesAL: I'm firmly on the side of ...
There's also a strong environmental case.

opinions.question: Do you agree or disagree with the following statement? It is more important for a company to keep its current customers than to attract new ones. Give specific reasons and examples to support your opinion.
opinions.model: I agree that keeping current customers is more important. There are two reasons. First, it costs less money. Companies spend a lot on ads to find new customers. Second, happy customers tell their friends about the company. For example, I have used the same phone company for ten years because their service is good. I also told my parents and my sister about it, and they joined too. So one happy customer can bring new customers. Also, if a company loses a customer, it is very hard to get them back. That's why I think keeping current customers is more important.
opinions.modelIH: I agree that it's more important for a company to keep its current customers, for two main reasons. First, keeping customers is much cheaper than finding new ones. Companies have to spend a lot of money on advertising and discounts to attract new people, but loyal customers keep buying without those costs. Second, satisfied customers often recommend the company to others. For example, I've used the same mobile phone company for ten years because their customer service is excellent. Whenever I have a problem, they solve it quickly. Because of that, I recommended them to my parents and my sister, and they both switched. In other words, one happy customer brought in two new ones for free. That's why I believe keeping current customers should come first.
opinions.modelAL: I agree that retaining existing customers should be a company's top priority. From a business perspective, it simply makes more financial sense. Attracting new customers requires heavy spending on advertising, promotions, and discounts, whereas loyal customers continue buying without that added cost. Even more valuable is the word-of-mouth effect. Satisfied customers become the company's best advertisers. Take my own experience. I've stayed with the same mobile carrier for ten years, largely because their customer service is outstanding. Whenever an issue comes up, it's resolved quickly and politely. As a result, I've recommended them to my parents and my sister, who both switched over. So by keeping me happy, the company gained two new customers at no cost. That's why I believe focusing on current customers is the smarter long-term strategy.

opinions.question: What do you think is the best way for a city to reduce air pollution: limiting the use of cars downtown, planting more trees, or giving money to people who buy electric cars? Give specific reasons and examples to support your opinion.
opinions.model: I think limiting the use of cars downtown is the best way. There are two reasons. First, cars are one of the main causes of air pollution in cities. If fewer cars come downtown, the air will be cleaner quickly. Second, it makes people use public transportation. For example, my city made a car-free street last year. Now people walk or take the bus there. The street is quieter and the air is better. Planting trees is good, but it takes a long time. Also, money for electric cars only helps people who can buy a new car. That's why I think limiting cars is the best way.
opinions.modelIH: I think limiting the use of cars downtown is the best way to reduce air pollution, for two reasons. First, cars are one of the biggest sources of air pollution in cities. If fewer cars enter the downtown area, the air quality will improve very quickly. Second, it encourages people to use public transportation, walk, or ride bikes. For example, last year my city turned one of its busiest downtown streets into a car-free zone on weekends. At first, some people complained, but now the street is full of people walking and shopping, and the air feels much fresher. Planting trees is helpful, but it takes many years to make a difference. And electric car money only helps people who can afford a new car. So limiting cars is the most effective option.
opinions.modelAL: Of the three options, I think restricting cars downtown would be the most effective. Vehicle exhaust is one of the main sources of urban air pollution, so reducing traffic in the busiest areas would have an immediate and measurable impact. It would also nudge people toward greener habits like taking public transportation, cycling, or walking. My city actually tried this last year by closing a major downtown street to cars on weekends. There was some resistance at first, but now the street is lively with pedestrians and outdoor cafés, and the air is noticeably fresher. Planting trees is worthwhile, but it takes years to make a real difference. Subsidies for electric cars, meanwhile, mainly benefit people who can already afford a new vehicle. Limiting cars delivers results faster and for everyone.

keyPhrasesAL: ... would have an immediate and measurable impact

opinions.question: Do you agree or disagree with the following statement? Employees who work from home are less productive than employees who work in an office. Give specific reasons and examples to support your opinion.
opinions.model: I disagree that people who work from home are less productive. There are two reasons. First, they don't waste time commuting. They can use that time to work or rest. Second, homes are often quieter than offices. For example, when I worked from home last year, I finished my reports faster. In the office, coworkers often talked to me, and I couldn't focus. At home, I could work without interruptions. Also, they can take short breaks at home, so they feel less tired. That's why I think people who work from home can be just as productive.
opinions.modelIH: I disagree that employees who work from home are less productive, for two reasons. First, they don't waste time and energy commuting. Many people spend two hours a day on the subway or in traffic, and when they work from home, they can use that time to start work earlier or simply rest. Second, home can be a better place to focus. For example, when I worked from home for six months last year, I actually finished my reports faster than before. In the office, coworkers often stopped by my desk to chat, and phones were ringing everywhere. At home, I could concentrate for hours without interruptions. Of course, some people find it hard to stay motivated at home, but with clear goals, remote workers can be just as productive.
opinions.modelAL: I disagree with this statement. In my experience, working from home can actually make people more productive. For a start, eliminating the commute frees up a lot of time and energy. Many workers spend up to two hours a day getting to and from the office, time that could be spent working or recharging. Also, offices are full of distractions. When I worked remotely for six months last year, I was surprised by how much faster I completed my reports. In the office, I was constantly interrupted by coworkers stopping by or by nearby phone calls, whereas at home I could concentrate deeply for hours at a time. That said, productivity at home depends on self-discipline and clear goals. With those in place, remote employees can easily match their office-based colleagues.
